title: Lavender sleep balm
subtitle: A wax-and-oil balm for temples, wrists, and pulse points
excerpt: Sleep balm is a firm wax-and-oil balm made with beeswax, shea butter, and coconut oil, fragranced with lavender and Roman chamomile essential oils. Applied to the temples, wrists, or chest before bed, body warmth releases the fragrance slowly throughout the night. Makes 50 g in a small tin; keeps twelve months in a cool cupboard.
sourceNotes: Lavender and Roman chamomile as a bedtime aromatic blend: The Complete Book of Essential Oils and Aromatherapy by Valerie Wormwood (1991, New World Library). Beeswax + shea + coconut as a solid-balm base: standard formulation documented in The Handmade Apothecary by Kim Walker and Vicky Chown (2017). Beeswax percentage at 15% produces a firm push-up or tin-stable balm at room temperature.

recipe.yieldDescription: ~50 g in a small screw-top tin or pot
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the recipe and fill multiple tins. Pour while still liquid, the balm sets very quickly once below 40°C.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Leave to set fully before sealing the tin. The scent softens slightly over the first week as the essential oils bind into the wax.
recipe.shelfLifeNotes: Twelve months in a cool, dark cupboard. Keep the lid on when not in use to protect the essential oil fragrance. Discard if the balm smells rancid or off.

glossaryTerms.definition: A cosmetic formula that contains no water. Balms are anhydrous, which means they do not need a preservative and can be stored at room temperature for months.

content.text: Melt the beeswax, shea butter, and coconut oil together in a heatproof bowl over a pan of simmering water. Stir until fully liquid. Remove from heat. Cool to 45°C, the mixture will still be liquid but no longer steaming. Add both essential oils and stir through. Pour immediately into a small screw-top tin or pot. Do not stir once poured: stirring while setting creates air bubbles. Leave to cool and harden fully at room temperature before sealing.

Apply a small amount to the inside of the forearm and wait 24 hours before applying to the face and neck. Roman chamomile can cause reactions in people who are sensitive to plants in the daisy family.
Twelve months in a cool, dark cupboard. Keep the lid on when not in use. Discard if the balm smells rancid or develops an off note.
